column1: # Where each Latin etymon in lex-la.tsv was checked.
# The etymon column of lex-la.tsv names an English word that came from a Latin
# one, and the product prints it three ways: "This is the Latin word your
# English X was borrowed from" on the word page, "Ancestor of English X" in
# the tooltip, and "English borrowed X from Y" in the discoveries feed. So it
# has to be true of X, and X is where it is checked.
# On 2026-10-03 all 319 were read against etymonline, against English
# Wiktionary for the six English words etymonline has no entry for, and
# against Lewis & Short where the English entry stops at a Latin derivative
# without saying what it was built on. 27 were not true as stated: 14 are
# removed, and 13 now name a word that did come from the headword. A
# fourteenth, timēre, gave its true etymon to timor and took timor's, so that
# each word sits on the row it came from. All are listed at the foot of this
# file with what the dictionary says, so that nobody restores one in good
# Each line names the entries it was checked against, separated by spaces:
#   ls:<key>            Lewis & Short, A Latin Dictionary (1879), by the entry's
#                       key in the Perseus text, as in la-notes.tsv:
# tests/tools/etymons.test.ts requires every etymon in lex-la.tsv to have a
# line here citing that English word's own entry, and no line here to
# outlive its claim. It cannot tell an entry somebody read from one somebody
# typed: cite the ones actually opened. etymonline files malic acid under
# malic, and the test knows that.
# What a borrowing survives, and what it does not
# Latin's verb is "borrowed", looser than Old English's "became", on purpose.
# It survives French, Italian or Spanish standing between the two: pork is
# Old French porc "and directly from Latin porcus". It survives the English
# word coming from a word built on the headword — a derivative, a diminutive,
# a compound: vaccine is from vaccīnus, from vacca; muscle from musculus,
# "a little mouse"; mellifluous from mellifluus, mel and fluere. And it
# survives a dictionary hesitating between two routes that both lead to the
# headword: saline is "probably from Latin salinum ... or salinae", both
# It does not survive the English word coming from a sibling, a word built on
# the same thing the headword was: ludicrous is from ludicrum, "from ludere",
# and lūdus is beside it; protect is from protegere, from tegere, and tēctum
# is beside it. An adverb is built on its adjective, so very, from vērus, is
# not from vērē. It does not survive a Latin word that only looks built on the
# headword and was taken from Greek on its own: Lewis & Short has nauticus
# "= ναυτικός", not nauta and -icus. And it does not survive "probably",
# "of uncertain origin" or "a merger" when the doubt is about the link to the
# headword, rather than about where the headword itself came from.
# Removed on 2026-10-03, with what the dictionary says
# Each was a claim lex-la.tsv made. A row keeps its note where it had one.
#   farmer   agricola     agriculture     etym:agriculture — from agricultura, "agri cultura", ager + cultura; ls:agricola1 is "ager-colo". Cousins
#   sailor   nauta        nautical        etym:nautical — from Latin nauticus, "from Greek nautikos"; ls:nauticus "= ναυτικός", ls:nauta "for navita, from navis"
#   goat     capra        capricious      etym:caprice — "a word of uncertain origin", Latin capreolus among "some guesses from 19c."; ls:capra is from caper
#   roof     tēctum       protect         etym:protect — from protegere, pro + "tegere"; ls:tectum is from tego. Siblings
#   church   ecclēsia     ecclesiastical  etym:ecclesiastic — from ecclesiasticus, "from Greek ekklesiastikos", from ekklesiastes; ls:ecclesiasticus "= ἐκκλησιαστικός"
#   land     terra        territory       etym:territory — "probably from Latin territorium", whose "rise ... is unexplained", or from "terrere 'to frighten'"; terra keeps terrain on its earth row
#   morning  māne         matinee         etym:matins — from matutinus, "associated with Matuta"; ls:matutinus is from Matuta, and ls:Matuta from the "root ma- of mane"
#   dream    somnium      somnolent       etym:somnolent — from somnolentus, "from somnus"; ls:somnium is from somnus too
#   oath     iūsiūrandum  jurisdiction    etym:jurisdiction — from "iuris dictio, genitive of ius"; ls:jusjurandum is built on ius as well
#   learn    discere      disciple        etym:disciple — discipulus "is of uncertain origin": from discere in OED and Watkins, not "according to Barnhart and Klein"
#   slowly   lentē        lento           etym:lento — from Italian lento, "from Latin lentus"; ls:lente is the adverb of lentus
#   quickly  celeriter    accelerate      etym:accelerate — from accelerare, ad + celerare, "from celer"; ls:celeriter is the adverb of celer
#   truly    vērē         very            etym:very — from Old French verai, from Vulgar Latin *veracus, "from Latin verax", "from verus"; ls:vere is the adverb of verus
#   hello    salvē        salvation       etym:salvation — from salvationem, "from ... salvare 'to save'"; ls:salve2 is the imperative of salveo. Cousins through salvus
# Replaced on 2026-10-03: the old etymon, the new one, and why
#   door      iānua      January → janitor             etym:january — from Ianuarius, "(the month) of Janus"; ls:januarius and ls:janua are both from Janus. etym:janitor — from ianitor, "from ianua"
#   floor     solum      soil → sole                   etym:soil — "a merger or confusion of three words in Old French"; etym:sole — from solea, "from solum"
#   river     flūmen     fluvial → flume               etym:fluvial — from fluvius, "related to fluere"; etym:flume — "from Latin flumen"
#   country   patria     patriot → repatriate          etym:patriot — from Late Latin patriota, "from Greek patriotes"; etym:repatriate — from repatriare, re- + "patria"
#   game      lūdus      ludicrous → interlude         etym:ludicrous — from ludicrum, "from ludere", where ls:ludicer says ludus; etym:interlude — inter + "ludus 'a play'"
#   fear      timor      timid → timorous              etym:timid — from timidus, "from timere"; etym:timorous — from timorosus, "from Latin timor"
#   fear      timēre     timorous → timid              the same two entries: each word now sits on the row it came from
#   joy       gaudium    gaudy → joy                   etym:gaudy — "probably" from gaud, "or possibly" from a Germanic plant name; etym:joy — from gaudia, "plural of gaudium"
#   hot       calidus    calorie → scald               etym:calorie — "from Latin calor"; etym:scald — from excaldare, ex + "calidus 'hot'"
#   red       ruber      ruby → rubric                 etym:ruby — from rubeus, "which is related to ruber"; etym:rubric — from rubrica, "from ruber"
#   remember  meminisse  memory → memento              etym:memory — from memoria, from memor, PIE *(s)mer-; etym:memento — "imperative of meminisse"
#   rise      surgere    surge → insurgent             etym:surge — "a word of uncertain origin, probably from French"; etym:insurgent — from insurgere, in- + "surgere"
#   always    semper     semper fidelis → sempiternal  a motto English quotes, with no entry as an English word; etym:sempiternal — from sempiternus, "from semper"
#   three     trēs       trio → trey                   etym:trio — Italian, "from tri-", "patterned on duo"; etym:trey — from Old French treis, "from Latin tria"
